title: Hydratation problem with react-instantsearch-nextjs and 2 InstantSearchNext components in the same page
body: ### 🐛 Current behavior Maybe I'm doing it wrong, but I need to have multiple instance of instant search in a page, with different configuration, using the same index. To reproduce, I took the next js app and changing it to only display 2 boxes, one displaying 4 Apple products, and one displaying 4 Hp products. as you can see there is an error, it's an hydration error. looking at the generated html, I can see 2 different objects attached to the same window property, I suspect it's the problem. ### 🔍 Steps to reproduce 1. Use the sandbox preview url https://lysjwf-3000.csb.app/ 2. observe the flickering on the top set of results 3. look at nextjs issue at the bottom left repo here https://github.com/stuff/instantsearch-nextjs-app-bug ### Live reproduction https://lysjwf-3000.csb.app/ ### 💭 Expected behavior No flickering, no hydration error ### Package version algoliasearch: 5.1.1, react-instantsearch: 7.22.1, react-instantsearch-nextjs: 1.0.11 ### Operating system _No response_ ### Browser _No response_ ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

comments.body:
Why are you not using two indices and a single InstantSearch component? with indexId passed you can use the same index multiple times.

InstantSearchNext indeed only works with a single InstantSearch instance.

That example is a very simplified version of my real use case. The real use case is that we do have a full react client side application we are migrating to nextjs, and we need SSR in most of the case (which are handled today by prerender.io)
So we have a lot of existing component which are totally autonomous, we can put them anywhere in the website, they currently embed their own InstantSearch, their own client, it could be any indices, with any configuration, even not the same api key (we use dynamic keys for logged users)

I've juste migrated them using InstantSearchNext instead of InstantSearch and expected to keep the same usage.

If not supported, I think the documentation should said it somewhere, because it's a step back from the regular client side only InstantSearch which we do use currently.

It's not really a regression, as previously neither InstantSearch instance was server-rendered and now one of them can be server-rendered. Unfortunately this is a simplification we had to make to make server side rendering work in nextjs

yes I understood that.

I'm going to look forward and use more the Index component in order to achieve what we want, and remove from SSR components that are not that important for SEO.

Thanks for the explanation and the hint about indexId I didn't knew.
